nodes.name: I.i.d. centred sub-Gaussian weights
nodes.statement: Let $\{\xi_{ij}\}_{i=1,\ldots,N_1\,,j=1,\ldots,N_2}$ a doubly indexed sequence of i.i.d. centred sub-Gaussian r.vs. with $$ E[\xi_{ij}\xi_{hk}]=\d_{ih}\d_{jk}\,, $$
nodes.statement_short: The disorder is a doubly indexed i.i.d. centred sub-Gaussian family with unit covariance.

nodes.name: High-load layer ratio
nodes.statement: For definiteness we assume that $$ \frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\to \a\in(0,1)\,. $$

nodes.name: P1) Marchenko-Pastur convergence of the sample covariance spectrum
nodes.statement: The empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law: $$ \frac{1}{N_1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_1}\d(\l-\l_i(\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T)) \rightharpoonup \r_{MP}(\l;\a)\quad \P-a.s. $$ where \be \r_{MP}(\l;\a):= (2-\frac{1}{\a})^+\d_0(\l) +\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2\pi \alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(\l-\l_-)(\l_+-\l)}}{\l}1_{[\l_-,\l_+]}(\l) \ee with $\l_{\pm}:=\left(1\pm\sqrt{\a/(1-\a)}\right)^2$.
nodes.statement_short: The empirical spectral measure of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law.
assumptions: rectangular random matrices with centred independent subgaussian entries with unitary variance
conclusions: The empirical distribution of the eigenvalues of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ converges a.s. to the Marchenko-Pastur law: $$ \frac{1}{N_1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_1}\d(\l-\l_i(\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T)) \rightharpoonup \r_{MP}(\l;\a)\quad \P-a.s. $$

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur law $\r_{MP}(\l;\a)$
nodes.statement_short: Explicit density of the Marchenko-Pastur law, with an atom at $0$ and support $[\l_-,\l_+]$.

nodes.name: P2) Localisation of the spectrum with large probability
nodes.statement: The spectrum of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T$ is localised in an interval with large probability: \be \P(\|\frac {1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\l_+}-1)\leq 2e^{-\frac {N_1t^2}{2}}\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Sub-Gaussian concentration confining the operator norm of $\frac{1}{N_2}\Xi\Xi^T-\mathbb I$.
assumptions: rectangular random matrices with centred independent subgaussian entries with unitary variance

nodes.name: Hopfield model and restricted Boltzmann machine Hamiltonians
nodes.statement: We will deal with two kind of Boltzmann machines: Hopfield models (HMs) and restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs). Their energy functions (or Hamiltonians) are \bea H_{N_1,N_2}^{HM}&:=&-\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\sum_{j=1}^{N_2}\sum_{i<k}^{N_1} \xi_{ij}\xi_{kj}x_ix_k \,,\\ H_{N_1,N_2}^{RBM}&:=&-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N_1+N_2}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_2}\sum_{i=1}^{N_1} \xi_{ij}x_iy_j\, \eea
nodes.statement_short: Energy functions of the Hopfield model (quadratic in one layer) and of the RBM (bilinear across two layers).

nodes.name: Spherical and Gaussian a priori measures $\s_{N,R}$, $\g_{N,\theta}$
nodes.statement: Let $S^{N}(R)$ be the $(N-1)$-dimensional sphere in $\R^N$ with radius $R\sqrt N$. Define the following a priori probability measures on $\R^N$: \be \begin{cases} \s_{N,R}(dx)&\mbox{uniform on $S^N(R)$}\,;\\ \g_{N,\theta}(dx)&\mbox{centred Gaussian with covariance $\theta \mathbb I$}\,. \end{cases} \ee

nodes.name: Regularised (sub-Gaussian) prior $\r_N$
nodes.statement: Models with Gaussian priors are typically ill-defined for low temperatures and need a sub-Gaussian regularisation. Let $r\,:\R\mapsto\R$ such that there is $\e>0$ with $$ \lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{r(x)}{x^{2+\e}}=\infty\,. $$ We define the regularised prior on $\R^N$ \be \r_N(dx):= e^{-Nr\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}\right)}\g_{N,\theta}(dx)\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: A Gaussian prior tilted by $e^{-Nr(\|x\|/\sqrt N)}$ with $r$ super-quadratic, to make low temperatures well defined.

nodes.name: Quartic choices of the regularising function $r$
nodes.statement: For instance in \cite{BDG} it was considered $r(x)=\b x^4/4$ while in \cite{gauss,legendre} $r(x)=\b x^4/4-\l x^2/2$.
nodes.origin_citation: Ben Arous, Dembo & Guionnet 2001; Barra, Genovese, Guerra & Tantari 2014; Genovese & Tantari 2015

nodes.name: Two-layer regularised prior $\r^2_{N_1,N_2}$
nodes.statement: This notion extends easily to two layer settings. We introduce some $r\,:\,\R^2\mapsto \R$ so that $$ \lim_{x^2+y^2\to\infty} \frac{r(x,y)}{x^2}=\lim_{x^2+y^2\to\infty} \frac{r(x,y)}{y^2}=\infty\,. $$ Then we define the following measure on $\R^{N_1}\times \R^{N_2}$ \be \r^2_{N_1,N_2}(dxdy):= e^{-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1},\frac{\|y\|}{\sqrt N_2}\right)}\g_{N_1,\theta}(dx)\g_{N_2,\theta}(dy)\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: The two-layer analogue of $\r_N$: a product Gaussian tilted by $e^{-\sqrt{N_1N_2}\,r(\cdot,\cdot)}$.

nodes.name: Low rank matrix factorisation as a two-layer regularisation
nodes.statement: A simple example is low rank matrix factorisation with Gaussian priors in which $r(x,y)=x^2y^2/2$ \cite{leo}.

nodes.name: Spherical shells $S_{N,R,\e}$ and the shell measure
nodes.statement: One technical problem is that the support of $\s_{N,R}$ has zero $\g_{N,\theta}$-measure, that is $\g_{N,\theta}(S^{N}(R))=0$. For this reason for a given $\e>0$ we need to introduce the spherical shells \be S_{N,R,\e}:=\{x\in\R^N\,:\,R-\e\leq\|x\|_2\leq R+\e\}\,. \ee We denote (here and further $|A|$ is the Lebesgue measure of the set $A$) $$ \s_{N,R.\e}(dx):=|S_{\e,N,R}|^{-1}1_{\{S_{\e,N,R}\}}(x)dx\, $$ the uniform probability on a shell and note that it is a.c. w.r.t. $\g_{N,\theta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Thickened spheres, introduced because the sphere itself is $\g_{N,\theta}$-null; carry the uniform measure and are absolutely continuous w.r.t. the Gaussian.

nodes.name: Surface expansion of a thin spherical shell
nodes.statement: We will also often make use of the simple relation \be |S_{\e,N,R}|=\e|S_{N,R}|+\OOO{\e^2}\,. \ee

nodes.name: Gibbs measures of the Boltzmann machines
nodes.statement: With these definitions at hand, we can introduce the probability distributions defining our Boltzmann machines. Let $\mu_{(\cdot)}\in\{\s_{(\cdot)},\g_{(\cdot)},\r_{(\cdot)}\}$ and $\mu^2_{(\cdot)}\in\{\s_{(\cdot)},\g_{(\cdot)}\}\otimes \{\s_{(\cdot)},\g_{(\cdot)}\}\cup\{\r_{(\cdot)}^2\}$ denote one prior among the one introduced before respectively for the one-layer and the bipartite machine. We have for $\b>0$ \be G^{HM}_{N_1,N_2,\b}(dx):=Z_{N_1,N_2,\b}^{-1}\mu_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\b H(x)}\,\qquad G^{RBM}_{N_1,N_2,\b}:=Z_{N_1,N_2,\b}^{-1}\mu^2_{N_1,N_2}(dxdy)e^{-\b H(x,y)}\,. \ee The normalisation $Z_{N_1,N_2,\b}$ is called partition function and it needs not to be the same, despite the symbol.
nodes.statement_short: Gibbs measures for the one-layer and bipartite machines, normalised by the partition function $Z_{N_1,N_2,\b}$.

nodes.name: Free energy of a Boltzmann machine
nodes.statement: Moreover \be A^{HM}_{N_1,N_2}(\b):=\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2,\b}\qquad A^{RBM}_{N_1,N_2}(\b):=\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2,\b}\,. \ee

nodes.name: Thermodynamic limit and the high-load regime
nodes.statement: Most interesting is to evaluate the last quantities in the so-called thermodynamic limit, namely $$ N_1,N_2\to\infty\,,\quad\mbox{such that }\qquad \lim_{N_1,N_2}\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}=:\a>0\,. $$ The regime $\a\neq0,1$ is called high-load and we will stick to that in this work.

nodes.name: Self-averaging of the free energy
nodes.statement: Being Lipschitz functions of the weights, free energies always satisfies a concentration inequality which ensures their a.s. convergence to the expected value. This self-averaging property will be exploited throughout without further mention.

nodes.name: Both layers carry the same prior parameters
nodes.statement: For simplicity we will assume always the distributions of the two layers to have the same parameters, \ie radius and variance. The general case requires a trivial extension of our formulas.

nodes.name: Marginalisation equivalence $HM_\s\leftrightarrow RBM_{\s,\g}$
nodes.statement: Marginalisation is the usual trick of RBMs. The two layers are coupled linearly, so that one can integrate out \'a la Stratonovich the units from the Gaussian layer in the partition function of a RBM to obtain the partition function of a HM (with $\b^2$ replacing $\b$). All the relevant quantities (e.g. Gibbs measures, free energy, order parameters etc) of one model can be computed directly from the one of the other one. For instance the equivalence $HM_\s\leftrightarrow RBM_{\s,\g}$ at the level of Gibbs measure reads as $$ Z^{-1}_{N_1,N_2,\b}\s_{N_2,R}(dx)\int_{\R^{N_2}}\g_{N_2,\theta}(dy)e^{\b H_{N_1,N_2}^{RBM}}=Z^{-1}_{N_1,N_2,\b}\s_{N_1,R}(dx)e^{\frac{\b^2}{\theta^2} H^{HM}_{N_1}}\,, $$ since the partition functions of the two models are numerically the same.
nodes.section: 1.2 Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Integrating out the Gaussian layer of an RBM turns its Gibbs measure into that of a Hopfield model with $\b^2$ in place of $\b$.
assumptions: The two layers are coupled linearly

nodes.name: Square radius and inverse variance as Legendre conjugates
nodes.statement: Legendre transforms are where the idea of equivalence of ensembles exploits and more precise statements are given in Theorem \ref{th:main} below. A Gaussian prior of $N$ units concentrates on a N-dimensional sphere of radius proportional to $\sqrt N$. To find the optimal radius we slice up the Gibbs measure at the level of the Gaussian prior and look for the most relevant contribution to the free energy. This strategy yields naturally a variational principle of the Legendre type relating the spherical and Gaussian free energies. Moreover we identify the square radius of the optimal sphere $R^2$ and the variance of the Gaussian model $\theta^{-1}$ as Legendre conjugate variables.
nodes.section: 1.2 Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Slicing the Gaussian prior by radius yields a Legendre variational principle in which $R^2$ and $\theta^{-1}$ are conjugate.

nodes.name: Heuristics for $RBM_{\s\s}\leftrightarrow RBM_{\r^2}$
nodes.statement: The main idea is very simple; we briefly outline the heuristics for the equivalence $RBM_{\s\s}\xleftrightarrow{LT} RBM_{\r^2}$ (the other cases are similar). By the standard disintegration of finite-dimensional Gaussian measures into spheres we have \bea &&\int_{\R^{N_1}\times \R^{N_1} }\mu^2(dxdy)e^{-\b H(x,y)}\nn\\ &=&\int_{0}^{\infty} dR_1\int_{0}^{\infty}dR_2 e^{-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{R_1}{\sqrt{N_1}},\frac{R_2}{\sqrt{N_2}}\right)-\frac{R_1}{2\theta_1}-\frac{R_2}{2\theta_2}}\nn\\ &&\frac{|S_{N_1}(R_1)\times S_{N_2}(R_2)|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1+N_2}}\int_{S_{N_1}(R_1)\times S_{N_2}(R_2)}\s_{N_1,R_1}(dx)\s_{N_2,R_2}(dy)e^{-\b H(x,y)}\,. \eea We adjusted the normalisation of the inner integral so to get the partition function of $RBM_{\s\s}$. Thus we continue the chain of identities as \be \eqref{eq:cont}=\int_{0}^{\infty} dR_1\int_{0}^{\infty}dR_2 e^{-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{R_1}{\sqrt{N_1}},\frac{R_2}{\sqrt{N_2}}\right)-\frac{R_1}{2\theta_1}-\frac{R_2}{2\theta_2}+\log\left(\frac{|S_{N_1}(R_1)\times S_{N_2}(R_2)|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1+N_2}}\right)+(N_1+N_2)A_{\s\s}(R_1,R_2)}\,. \ee Then we can evaluate the integral by the usual Laplace method, since by a simple scaling argument the maximum must be attained at the scale $R_1,R_2\sim\sqrt{N_1+N_2}$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Disintegrate the Gaussian priors into spheres, recognise the doubly spherical partition function inside, then apply Laplace's method in the two radii.

nodes.name: Ingredients needed to make the heuristics rigorous
nodes.statement: To give rigorous grounds to this heuristics we need some few properties. First, we have to control the thermodynamic limit of the free energy of spherical models $HM_\s$ and $RBM_{\s\s}$. These limits are computed in Section \ref{section:sferico}. Secondly, to properly implement the above disintegration formula, we need the regular behaviour of the model with spherical shell prior as the thickness of the shell vanish. In other words, at the level of free energy thermodynamics should favour those configurations on the shell which actually lie on a given sphere into it. This is proven in sections \ref{section:sferico} and \ref{section:legendre}. Lastly, the unit configurations outside any ball of radius growing faster than $\sqrt N_1, \sqrt N_2$ must give vanishing contribution in the thermodynamic limit. This is proven in Section \ref{section:legendre}, where the proof of our main result, \ie subsequent Theorem \ref{th:main}, is completed.
nodes.section: 1.2 Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: Three ingredients are required: the spherical thermodynamic limits, shell-to-sphere regularity, and negligibility of far tails.

nodes.name: Legendre equivalences of the free energies
nodes.statement: Assume $\bf P1), P2)$ and let $\r_N, \r^2_N$ be defined as in (\ref{eq:Reg-prior1}), (\ref{eq:Reg-prior2}) and discussion around. Then \begin{itemize} \item[i)] $HM_{\s}\xleftrightarrow{LT} HM_{\r}$: \be A_\r(\theta,\a,\b)=\a \sup_{R>0}\left( \a^{-1}A_{\s}(R,\b) -\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\log R- r(R) -\frac12(\log\theta-1) \right)\,; \ee \be A_{\s}(R,\b)=\a \inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\a^{-1}A_\r(\theta,\a,\b) -\log R+ r(R)+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,. \ee \item[ii)] $RBM_{\s\s}\xleftrightarrow{LT} RBM_{\s,\g}$: \be A_{\s,\g}(\theta,R_2,\a,\b)=\a\sup_{R_1>0}\left(\a^{-1}A_{\s\s}(R_1,R_2,\b)-\frac{R_1^2}{2\theta}+\log R_1 -\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,; \ee \be A_{\s\s}(R_1,R_2,\b)=\a\inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R_1^2}{2\theta}+\a^{-1}A_{\s,\g}(\theta,R_2,\a,\b)-\log R_1+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,. \ee \item[iii)] $RBM_{\s\s}\xleftrightarrow{LT} RBM_{\r^2}$: \be A_{\r^2}(\theta,\a,\b)=\sup_{R_1,R_2>0}\left(A_{\s\s}(R_1,R_2)-\frac{\a R_1^2+(1-\a)R_2^2}{2\theta}+\log(R_1^\a R_2^{1-\a})-\sqrt{\a(1-\a)}r(R_1,R_2)-\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,; \ee \be A(R_1,R_2)=\inf_{\theta_1,\theta_2>0}\left(\frac{\a R_1^2}{2\theta_1}+\frac{(1-\a)R_2^2}{2\theta_2}+A_{\r^2}(\theta_1,\theta_2,\a,\b)-\log(R_1^\a R_2^{1-\a})+\sqrt{\a(1-\a)}r(R_1,R_2)+\frac12(\log\theta_1^\a\theta_2^{1-\a}-1)\right)\,. \ee \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 1.2 Main result and organisation of the paper
nodes.statement_short: The free energies of the spherical and (sub-)Gaussian Hopfield models and RBMs are related pairwise by explicit Legendre transforms in the radius / variance.
assumptions: let $\r_N, \r^2_N$ be defined as in (\ref{eq:Reg-prior1}), (\ref{eq:Reg-prior2}) and discussion around
conclusions: \item[i)] $HM_{\s}\xleftrightarrow{LT} HM_{\r}$: \be A_\r(\theta,\a,\b)=\a \sup_{R>0}\left( \a^{-1}A_{\s}(R,\b) -\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\log R- r(R) -\frac12(\log\theta-1) \right)\,; \ee \be A_{\s}(R,\b)=\a \inf_{\theta>0}\left(\frac{R^2}{2\theta}+\a^{-1}A_\r(\theta,\a,\b) -\log R+ r(R)+\frac12(\log\theta-1)\right)\,. \ee

nodes.name: Remaining equivalences and the Gibbs-measure level
nodes.statement: The other equivalences of the scheme above can be derived by combining $i), ii), iii)$ and marginalisations. Albeit we will not include that in this paper, these dualities can be established also for the Gibbs distributions (\ref{eq:Gibbs}).

nodes.name: Comparison with previous results on the bipartite spherical model
nodes.statement: Previous results on the model have been obtained in \cite{AC} and \cite{baik1}. In \cite{baik1} the authors achieve the same result as in our Theorem \ref{Th:Bip-sfer} and prove much more: fluctuations of the free energy are shown to be Gaussian in high temperature and Tracy-Widom for low temperature. The assumptions on the weight distribution are more general then ours, as they only require finiteness of the moments. Yet the method there employed is a sophisticated and technical random matrix argument and our approach is certainly lighter and more accessible to non-specialists. In \cite{AC} a variational principle for the free energy has been proven only for small $\b$, by means of the so-called Latala method.
nodes.statement_short: Baik & Lee obtain the same free energy plus fluctuations by random matrix methods; Auffinger & Chen only cover small $\b$ via Latala's method.

nodes.name: Why is the doubly spherical RBM free energy fully convex?
nodes.statement: In any case it is remarkable that the free energy of a doubly spherical RBM satisfies a fully convex minimisation principle, which is a crucial difference compared to the $\min\max$ of Gauss-Bernoulli \cite{bgg} and Bernoulli-Bernoulli RBMs \cite{Bip}. The reason for that eludes our current understanding and we must defer the discussion of this point to future works.
nodes.statement_short: The reason a doubly spherical RBM gives a convex minimisation rather than a $\min\max$ is left unexplained.

nodes.name: Free energy of the spherical Hopfield model $HM_\s$
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\s}$. It holds $P$-a.s. \be \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} = \a\min_{2q\geq \b(1-\a)\l_+}\left(q R^2 -\frac 12\int\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log(2q-\b(1-\a)\l) d\l-\log R-\frac12\right)\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: The $HM_\s$ free energy converges a.s. to a one-dimensional convex minimisation over $q$ against the Marchenko-Pastur law.
assumptions: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\s}$.

nodes.name: Free energy of the doubly spherical RBM $RBM_{\s\s}$
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $RBM_{\s\s}$ and $\a\leq \frac 12$. It holds $P$-a.s. \begin{eqnarray} \lim_{N_1,N_2\to\infty} A_{N_1,N_2} &=&\min_{ab\geq \b^2(1-\a)\l_+}\left(\frac{R^2}{2}\left(\a a + (1-\a) b\right) -\frac 1 2 (1-2\a)\log(b)\right. \nonumber \\ &-&\left.\frac \a2\int\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log(ab-\b^2(1-\a)\l) d\l-\log R-\frac12\right) \,. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: For $\a\le 1/2$ the $RBM_{\s\s}$ free energy converges a.s. to a jointly convex minimisation in the two Lagrange multipliers $a,b$.
assumptions: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ denote the free energy of $RBM_{\s\s}$ and $\a\leq \frac 12$.

nodes.name: The restriction $\a\leq\frac12$ is only a convenience
nodes.statement: The choice $\a\leq\frac12$ is just a matter of convenience as it will be clear that pre-choosing the largest layer simplifies a lot the notations. For $\alpha\geq \frac12$ one should bear in mind that the Marchenko-Pastur distribution (\ref{eq:MP}) has an atom in zero.

nodes.name: Shell priors approximate the spherical prior
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\s_\e}$, $RBM_{\s_\e\s}$ or $RBM_{\s_\e\s_\e}$. Then it is $$ \lim_{\e\to0}\lim_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}=\lim_{N_1,N_2}\lim_{\e\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: The shell-thickness limit and the thermodynamic limit of the free energy commute.
assumptions: Let $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}$ denote the free energy of $HM_{\s_\e}$, $RBM_{\s_\e\s}$ or $RBM_{\s_\e\s_\e}$.

nodes.name: Proof that shell priors approximate the spherical prior
nodes.statement: In this proof we write $N$ to mean $N_1$ or $N_2$ and by $A^{\s}(R; \b)$ the free energy of a spherical model of radius $R$, according to the context. No further details are needed. By Fubini and the mean value theorem there is a $R^*_\e\in[R\sqrt N-\e,R\sqrt N+\e]$ for which $$ \widehat A_{N_1,N_2}=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\s}(R^*_\e; \b)\,. $$ By a simple change of variables we have $$ A_{N_1,N_2}^{\s}(R^*_\e; \b)=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\s}(R; c_{N,\e}\b)\,, $$ with $c_{N,\e}:=R^2_\e/R^2N$. Therefore by Lipschitz continuity of the free energy w.r.t. $\b$ $$ |A^\s_{N_1,N_2}-\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}|\leq \frac\e N\,. $$ This, combined with $A^\s_{N_1,N_2}=\lim_{\e\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}$, gives the assert.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem picks a radius inside the shell, a rescaling turns it into a shift of $\b$, and Lipschitz continuity bounds the gap by $\e/N$.

nodes.statement_short: Fix notation for the spherical free energy at a given radius.

nodes.name: Mean value theorem on the shell
nodes.statement: By Fubini and the mean value theorem there is a $R^*_\e\in[R\sqrt N-\e,R\sqrt N+\e]$ for which $$ \widehat A_{N_1,N_2}=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\s}(R^*_\e; \b)\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Fubini plus the mean value theorem realise the shell free energy as a spherical one at some radius $R^*_\e$.

nodes.name: Change of variables in the radius
nodes.statement: By a simple change of variables we have $$ A_{N_1,N_2}^{\s}(R^*_\e; \b)=A_{N_1,N_2}^{\s}(R; c_{N,\e}\b)\,, $$ with $c_{N,\e}:=R^2_\e/R^2N$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescaling the sphere trades the shifted radius for a rescaled inverse temperature $c_{N,\e}\b$.

nodes.name: Lipschitz continuity concludes
nodes.statement: Therefore by Lipschitz continuity of the free energy w.r.t. $\b$ $$ |A^\s_{N_1,N_2}-\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}|\leq \frac\e N\,. $$ This, combined with $A^\s_{N_1,N_2}=\lim_{\e\to0} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}$, gives the assert.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz continuity in $\b$ gives an $O(\e/N)$ gap, which yields the interchange of limits.

nodes.name: Diagonalisation of the Hopfield energy under a spherical prior
nodes.statement: The best advantage of the spherical prior is that one can diagonalise the energy (\ref{eq:HM}): $$ H(x)=-(1-\a)\sum_{i=1}^{N_1}\l_ix_i^2\,. $$

nodes.name: Gaussian upper bound on the shell partition function
nodes.statement: Let $2q>\b(1-\a)\l_+$. Then using (\ref{eq:shells-surface}) we have \bea \e \hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\e}(\b,\a,R)&=& \e\ e^{q R^2 N_1}\int_{\R^{N_1}}\s_{N_1,R,\e}(dz)e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\b(1-\a)}{2}\l_i)z_i^2}\\ &\leq&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\R^N}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(2q-\b(1-\a)\l_i)z_i^2/2}\nn\\ &=&e^{q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N}}|}e^{-\frac 12\sum_i^N\log(2q-\b(1-\a)\l_i)}\nn\,, \eea
nodes.statement_short: Bound the shell integral by a full Gaussian integral and evaluate it exactly.

nodes.name: Pass to the trial function $\tilde A(q)$
nodes.statement: therefore, since $\frac 1{N_1} \log \left(|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}| /\sqrt{2\pi}^{N_1} \right) \to \log R +\frac 1 2$ and thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac1{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\b,\a,R)\leq \a q R^2 -\frac \a2\int\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log(2q-\b(1-\a)\l)-\a\log R-\frac\a2=:\tilde A(q)\,, $$ whence, as $\tilde A(q)$ is continuous, $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}\frac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}(\b,\a,R)\leq\min_{2q\geq\b(1-\a)\l_+}\tilde A(q). $$
nodes.statement_short: Take the thermodynamic limit and optimise over $q$ to get the upper bound $\min_q\tilde A(q)$.

nodes.name: Convexity and uniqueness of the minimiser
nodes.statement: Moreover for $2q>\b(1-\a)\l_+$ $$ \partial_q^2 \tilde A(q)=2\a\int d\l\frac{\r_{MP}(\l;\a)}{(2q-\b(1-\a)\l)^2}>0, $$ thus $\tilde A(q)$ is convex and the minimum is attained in a unique point $\bar q$.
nodes.statement_short: The second derivative is positive, so $\tilde A$ is convex with a unique minimiser $\bar q$.

nodes.name: Set up the reverse bound
nodes.statement: \ni Now the reverse bound. Let $\e>0$ and $S^c_{N_1,R,\e}$ the complementary set of the shell $S_{N_1,R,\e}$. It holds $$ \e \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}=e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{\R^{N_1}}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}{2}}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\b(1-\a)}{2}\l_i)z_i^2}-e^{ q R^2 N_1}\frac{(2\pi)^{\frac N2}}{|S_{R\sqrt{N_1}}|}\int_{S_{N_1,R,\e}^c}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\b(1-\a)}{2}\l_i)z_i^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Write the shell partition function as the full Gaussian integral minus the integral over the shell complement.

nodes.name: Bound the complement integral by exponential tilting
nodes.statement: For any $\eta>0$ small enough we have \bea \int_{S_{N_1,R,\e}^c}\frac{dz}{(2\pi)^{\frac {N_1}2}} e^{-\sum_i^{N_1}(q-\frac{\b(1-\a)}{2}\l_i)z_i^2}&\leq&\exp\left[N_1\left(\eta\left(R^2-\frac\e {N_1}\right)-\frac{1}{2N_1}\sum_j\log(2q-\b\l_j+2\eta)\right)\right]\nn\\ &+&\exp\left[N_1\left(-\eta\left(R^2+\frac\e {N_1}\right)-\frac{1}{2N_1}\sum_j\log(2q-\b\l_j-2\eta)\right)\right]\nn. \eea
nodes.statement_short: Tilt by $\pm\eta$ to bound the complement by two exponential terms.

nodes.name: Identify the relevant shell scale and the competing exponents
nodes.statement: \ni Note now that the r.h.s. is $o(e^{-N})$ if $\frac\e N\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$. So the greatest contribution is at the scale $\e=\tilde\e N$, $\tilde\e>0$ independent on $N_1$. Therefore \be \lim\inf_{N_1,N_2}\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\tilde\e}\geq\max\left(\tilde A(q), A^1_{\tilde\e}(\eta; q), A^2_{\tilde\e}(\eta; q)\right), \ee with \bea A^1_{\tilde\e}(\eta; q)&=&\a(q+\eta)R^2-\a\tilde\e\eta-\frac\a2\int d\l\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log(2(q+\eta)-\b\l)-\a\log R-\frac\a2;\\ A^2_{\tilde\e}(\eta; q)&=&\a(q-\eta)R^2-\a\tilde\e\eta-\frac\a2\int d\l\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log(2(q-\eta)-\b\l)-\a\log R-\frac\a2. \eea
nodes.statement_short: The dominant scale is $\e=\tilde\e N$, giving a max of $\tilde A$ against two tilted functionals $A^1,A^2$.

nodes.name: Reduce to showing the trial value dominates
nodes.statement: Now we show that if $\bar q$ is the unique minimiser of $\tilde A(q)$ it is for $\eta$ small enough $$ \tilde A(\bar q)=\max\left(\tilde A(\bar q), A^1_{\tilde\e}(\eta; \bar q), A^2_{\tilde\e}(\eta; \bar q)\right)\,, $$ which will conclude the proof.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to show $\tilde A(\bar q)$ dominates the two tilted functionals for small $\eta$.

nodes.name: Sign analysis of the differences $\D_\pm$
nodes.statement: To do so we introduce \bea \D_-(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^1_{\tilde\e}(\eta; q)= -\a\eta(R^2-\tilde\e)+\frac\a2\int d\l\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log\left(\frac{2(q+\eta)-\b\l}{2q-\b\l}\right);\\ \D_+(q;\eta)&:=&\tilde A(q)-A^2_{\tilde\e}(\eta; q)= \a\eta(R^2+\tilde\e)+\frac\a2\int d\l\r_{MP}(\l;\a)\log\left(\frac{2(q-\eta)-\b\l}{2q-\b\l}\right)\,. \eea \ni As a function of $\eta$, $\D_\pm(q;\eta)$ are continuous and differentiable, vanishing in $\eta=0$ and with $\lim_{\eta\to+\infty}\D_\pm(q,\eta)=\pm\infty$. Moreover $\D_+(q;\eta)$ is uniformly convex and $\D_-(q;\eta)$ uniformly concave. Thus $\D_-(q;\eta)$ assumes a positive maximum iff the derivative in $\eta=0$ is positive, that is \be 0<-(R^2-\tilde\e)+\int d\l\frac{\r_{MP}(\l;\a)}{2q-\b\l}=\tilde \e-\partial_q \tilde A(q)\,. \ee \ni Likewise for $\D_+(q;\eta)$ is always positive iff $\left.\partial_\eta \D_+(q;\eta)\right|_{\eta=0}\geq0$, \ie \be 0\leq(R^2+\tilde\e)+\int d\l\frac{\r_{MP}(\l;\a)}{2q-\b\l}=\tilde \e+\partial_q \tilde A(q). \ee
nodes.statement_short: Convexity/concavity of $\D_\pm$ in $\eta$ turns the claim into two sign conditions on $\partial_q\tilde A$.

nodes.name: Conclude at the stationary point
nodes.statement: Combining (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi1}) and (\ref{eq:upper-bound-epsi2}) we get $$ -\tilde\e\leq \left.\partial_q \tilde A(q)\right|_{q=\tilde q}<\tilde\e\,,, $$ that is $\tilde q$ is the unique stationary point of $\tilde A(q)$. With this choice of $q$, relation (\ref{eq:max( , , )}) gives \be \lim\inf_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2.\tilde \e}\geq \min_{q\geq\b\l_+}\tilde A(q) \,. \ee As $\tilde\e$ can be taken arbitrarily small, we recover (\ref{eq:AHMsfer}).
nodes.statement_short: The two conditions pin $q$ to the stationary point, and letting $\tilde\e\to0$ recovers the claimed formula.

nodes.name: Singular value decomposition of the RBM energy
nodes.statement: First step is to use the singular value decomposition of the matrix $\{\xi_{ij}\}$ to write \be \frac{1}{\sqrt{N_1+N_2}}(x,\xi y)=\sqrt{1-\a}\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i\,, \ee where $\tilde x,\tilde y$ are related respectively to $x,y$ by an orthogonal transformation. Note that this decomposition removes automatically $N_2-N_1$ cyclic coordinates of the second layer.
nodes.statement_short: An orthogonal change of variables diagonalises the bilinear RBM coupling into $\sqrt{1-\a}\sum_i\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i$.

nodes.name: The top singular value contributes exponentially little
nodes.statement: There exists $c,C>0$ so that $$E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>\bar\s\}}]\leq Ce^{-cN_1}\,,$$ where $\bar \s:= 1+\sqrt{\frac{\a}{1+\a}}$.

nodes.name: Proof that the top singular value is negligible
nodes.statement: For any $a>\bar\s$ we compute $$ E[e^{\a\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]=E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\leq a\}}]+E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>a\}}]\,. $$ The first summand is easily estimated by \be E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\leq a\}}]\leq E[e^{\b a\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]\leq E[e^{\b a \|\tilde x\|\|\tilde y\|}]\,. \ee Arguing as in the proof of \cite[Proposition 1]{legendre} we can write for a $C>0$ \be E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>a\}}]\leq Ca\sqrt{2\pi (N_1+N_2)}e^{\frac{\b^2}{2(N_1+N_2)}\|\tilde x\|^2\|\tilde y\|^2}\,. \ee Then (\ref{eq:bound1}) and (\ref{eq:bound2}) give an annealed bound for the free energy: \be \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_N\leq \max\left(\bar\s\b\sqrt{\a(1-\a)}R^2\,,\,\,\frac12 \b^2\a(1-\a)R^2_1R^2_2 \right)<\infty\,. \ee With this bound at hand, we repeat mutatis mutandis the steps of the proof of \cite[Lemma 1]{legendre} to get \be E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>\bar\s\}}]\leq\sqrt{\a(1-\a)\b^2R^4+a^2}\sqrt{P(\|\Xi\Xi^T/N_2-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\l_+}-1)} \ee and the assert follows from (\ref{eq:impo-spectrum}).
nodes.statement_short: Split the annealed exponential moment at the threshold $a$, bound each piece, then use the spectral concentration P2).

nodes.name: Split at the singular value threshold
nodes.statement: For any $a>\bar\s$ we compute $$ E[e^{\a\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]=E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\leq a\}}]+E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>a\}}]\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Split the exponential moment according to whether the largest singular value exceeds $a$.

nodes.name: Bound the small-singular-value summand
nodes.statement: The first summand is easily estimated by \be E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\leq a\}}]\leq E[e^{\b a\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}]\leq E[e^{\b a \|\tilde x\|\|\tilde y\|}]\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: On the good event replace $\s_i$ by $a$ and use Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Bound the large-singular-value summand
nodes.statement: Arguing as in the proof of \cite[Proposition 1]{legendre} we can write for a $C>0$ \be E[e^{\b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i\tilde x_i\tilde y_i}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>a\}}]\leq Ca\sqrt{2\pi (N_1+N_2)}e^{\frac{\b^2}{2(N_1+N_2)}\|\tilde x\|^2\|\tilde y\|^2}\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Import the estimate of Genovese & Tantari for the bad event.

nodes.name: Annealed bound for the free energy
nodes.statement: Then (\ref{eq:bound1}) and (\ref{eq:bound2}) give an annealed bound for the free energy: \be \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_N\leq \max\left(\bar\s\b\sqrt{\a(1-\a)}R^2\,,\,\,\frac12 \b^2\a(1-\a)R^2_1R^2_2 \right)<\infty\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Combining the two estimates gives a finite annealed bound on the free energy.

nodes.name: Conclude via the spectral concentration
nodes.statement: With this bound at hand, we repeat mutatis mutandis the steps of the proof of \cite[Lemma 1]{legendre} to get \be E[A_{N_1,N_2}1_{\{\max_{i\in[N_1]}\s_i>\bar\s\}}]\leq\sqrt{\a(1-\a)\b^2R^4+a^2}\sqrt{P(\|\Xi\Xi^T/N_2-\mathbb I\|_{op}\geq t+\sqrt{\l_+}-1)} \ee and the assert follows from (\ref{eq:impo-spectrum}).
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz against the P2) tail bound yields the exponential decay.

Now start from (ef{eq:diagRBM}) and write for any $a,b$ such that $ab> ^2(1-\a)\l_+$  ea Z_{N_1,N_2}&=&\int\s_1(dx)\s_2(dy) \exp\left( \sqrt{1-\a}  \sum_{i\in[N_1]}x_iy_i\s_i- rac a2 \|x\|^2- rac b2 \|y\|^2+ rac a2 R^2N_1+ rac b2 R^2N_2ight)
n\ &=&\exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)ight) \int\s_1(dx)\s_2(dy)\exp\left( - rac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)ight)\,, \eea where we have defined $$ z^T_i :=  egin{cases} (x_i,y_i)&i=1,\ldots , N_1\,,\ (0,y_i)&i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2 \end{cases}$$ and the $2	imes 2$ symmetric positively defined matrix $$ M_i := \left( { egin{array}{cc} a & - \sqrt{1-\a}\s_i \ - \sqrt{1-\a}\s_i & b \ \end{array} } ight)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]\qquad M_i:=\diag(0,b)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,. $$ Thus by (ef{eq:shells-surface})  ea \e^2\hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\e}&\leq& \exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)ight)  rac{(2\pi)^{ rac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{ rac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} \int  rac{dx dy}{\sqrt{2\pi}^N}\exp\left( - rac 12\sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)ight),
n\ &=& \exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)ight)  rac{(2\pi)^{ rac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{ rac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} b^{- rac{N_2-N_1}{2}} \prod_{i=1}^{N_1}(ab- ^2(1-\a)\s^2_i)^{- rac 12}\,. \eea We introduce  e  ar A(a,b):=  rac {R^2}{2} (a\a+b(1-\a))-\log R- rac12- rac{1-2\a}{2}\log b - rac{\a}{2}\int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\log(ab-(1-\a) ^2\l)\,. \ee and $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq  ar A(a,b)\,,\quad  orall a,b>0\,:\,\,ab>(1-\a) ^2\l_+\,. $$ A direct inspection shows that $A(a,b)$ is jointly uniformly convex for any $\a\in[0,1/2]$ if $ab>(1-\a) ^2\l_+$, therefore  e \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \min_{ab>(1-\a) ^2\l_+}  ar A(a,b)\,. \ee We record for later use the gradient coordinates  ea \partial_a  ar A(a,b)&=& rac{\a R^2}{2}- rac\a2\int _{MP}(d\l;\a) rac{b}{ab- (1-\a) ^2\l}\,;\ \partial_b  ar A(a,b)&=& rac{(1-\a)R^2}{2} - rac{1-2\a}{2b}- rac\a2\int _{MP}(d\l;\a) rac{a}{ab- (1-\a) ^2\l}\,. \eea For the reverse bound consider again spherical shells around $S_{R,N_1}$ and $S_{R,N_2}$ of thickness $\e$, that we name respectively $S_{1,\e}$ and $S_{2,\e}$. We split $S_{1,\e}=\R^{N_1}\setminus S^c_{1,\e}$ and $S_{2,\e}=\R^{N_2}\setminus S^c_{2,\e}$ and set $S_{\e}:=S_{1,\e}	imes S_{2,\e}$. We have  ea \e^2 \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}&:=&\e^2\int\s_{N_1, R,\e}(dx)\s_{N_2,R,\e}(dy)e^{-  H_N(x,y)}
n\ &=&\exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)ight) \int_{\R^{N_1}	imes \R^{N_2}}  rac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( - rac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)ight)
n\ &-&\exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)ight) \int_{S^c_{\e}}  rac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( - rac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)ight)\,, \eea where we used again the representation (ef{eq:repr-Z-RBM}). The free energy associated to the first summand was already computed above in the thermodynamic limit. Therefore we have to upper bound the second summand. We consider four contributions according to the following decomposition. Let $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and put  ea S_\e^{\kappa,1}&:=&\{x\in\R^{N_1}\,, y\in\R^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|x\|^2-R^2N_1)\geq \e N_1\,\}\,,
n\ S_\e^{\kappa,2}&:=&\{x\in\R^{N_1}\,, y\in\R^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|y\|^2-R^2N_2)\geq \e N_2\,\}\,.
n \eea Thus $S_\e^c= igcup_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}}S_\e^{\kappa,j}$. Moreover we pick $\eta>0$ small enough and set  ea M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) &:=& \left( { egin{array}{cc} a+(2-j)\kappa\eta & - \sqrt{1-\a}\s_i \ - \sqrt{1-\a}\s_i & b+(j-1)\kappa\eta \ \end{array} } ight)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]
n\ M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta)&:=&\diag(0,b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.
n \eea Also, we put  ea Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}^{\kappa,j}&:=& \exp\left( rac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)+ rac{(2-j)N_1\kappa\eta a}{2}+ rac{(j-1)N_2\kappa\eta b}{2}-\eta \e N_jight)
n\ &&\int_{S_\e^{\kappa,j}}  rac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( - rac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) z_i)ight)
n\ \eea so that $$ (ef{eq:II-termRBM})=-\sum_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j=1,2} Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}^{\kappa,j}\,. $$ We conclude that for any $\eta>0$ sufficiently small and $a,b$ with $ab>(1-\a) ^2\l_+$  e \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\geq \max( ar A(a,b), \{A_\e^{\kappa, j}(\eta; a,b)\}_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}})\,, \ee where  ea A_\e^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)&:=&-\eta\e+ rac12\a a(R^2+(2-j)\kappa\eta)+ rac12(1-\a) b(R^2+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
n\ &-&\log R - rac12- rac{1-2\a}{2}\log (b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
n\ &-& rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\log((a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\a) ^2\l)\,. 
n \eea In analogy with the proof of Theorem ef{Th:HM-sfer} we define  ea \D_{\e}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)&:=& ar A(a,b)-A_\e^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)
n\ &=&\eta \e-(2-j)\kappa rac{\eta\a a}{2}-(j-1)\kappa rac{\eta(1-\a) b}{2}+ rac{1-2\a}{2}\log(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
n\ &+& rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\log\left( rac{(a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\a) ^2\l}{ab-(1-\a) ^2\l}ight)\,.
n \eea We need to show that $\D_{\e}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)\geq0$ for $\eta>0$ small. As before, to do so it suffices to prove the derivative in the origin to be non-negative uniformly in $\e>0$. Bearing in mind (ef{eq:grad1RBM}), (ef{eq:grad2RBM}) we have  ea  rac{d}{d\eta} \D_{\e}^{\kappa,j}(\eta) ig|_{\eta=0}&=&\e+(2-j)\kappa\left(- rac{a\a R^2}{2}+ rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\left( rac{b}{ab-(1-\a) ^2\l}ight)ight)
n\ &+&(j-1)\kappa\left(- rac{b(1-\a) R^2}{2}+ rac{1-2\a}{2b}+ rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\left( rac{a}{ab-(1-\a) ^2\l}ight)ight)
n\ &=&\e-(2-j)\kappa\partial_a ar A-(j-1)\kappa\partial_b ar A\geq0\,. 
n \eea Since the inequality must hold for any $\e>0$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, we have to pick $( ar a,  ar b)=\arg\min  ar A$. Therefore $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\geq \max( ar A( ar a, ar b), \{A^{\e,\kappa_1,\kappa_2}(\eta;  ar a, ar b)\}_{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\{-1,1\}})= \min_{ab> ^2(1-\a)\l_+} ar A( a, b)\quad  orall \e>0\,, $$ which combined with (ef{eq:upperbound.RBM}) proves the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Two Lagrange multipliers $a,b$ turn the doubly spherical partition function into $2\times2$ Gaussian blocks; the convex trial function $\bar A(a,b)$ bounds above and a four-region tilt argument matches it below.

nodes.name: Gaussian block representation of the partition function
nodes.statement: Now start from (\ref{eq:diagRBM}) and write for any $a,b$ such that $ab>\b^2(1-\a)\l_+$ \bea Z_{N_1,N_2}&=&\int\s_1(dx)\s_2(dy) \exp\left( \sqrt{1-\a} \b\sum_{i\in[N_1]}x_iy_i\s_i-\frac a2 \|x\|^2-\frac b2 \|y\|^2+\frac a2 R^2N_1+\frac b2 R^2N_2\right)\nn\\ &=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int\s_1(dx)\s_2(dy)\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\,, \eea where we have defined $$ z^T_i := \begin{cases} (x_i,y_i)&i=1,\ldots , N_1\,,\\ (0,y_i)&i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2 \end{cases}$$ and the $2\times 2$ symmetric positively defined matrix $$ M_i := \left( {\begin{array}{cc} a & -\b\sqrt{1-\a}\s_i \\ -\b\sqrt{1-\a}\s_i & b \\ \end{array} } \right)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]\qquad M_i:=\diag(0,b)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce multipliers $a,b$ and rewrite the partition function through $2\times2$ matrices $M_i$.

nodes.name: Upper bound by determinants
nodes.statement: Thus by (\ref{eq:shells-surface}) \bea \e^2\hat{Z}_{N_1,N_2,\e}&\leq& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \frac{(2\pi)^{\frac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{\frac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} \int \frac{dx dy}{\sqrt{2\pi}^N}\exp\left( -\frac 12\sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right),\nn\\ &=& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \frac{(2\pi)^{\frac{N_1}{2}} (2\pi)^{\frac{N_2}{2}} }{S^R_{N_1} S^R_{N_2}} b^{-\frac{N_2-N_1}{2}} \prod_{i=1}^{N_1}(ab-\b^2(1-\a)\s^2_i)^{-\frac 12}\,. \eea
nodes.statement_short: Relax the shell integral to $\R^{N_1+N_2}$ and evaluate the Gaussian determinants.

nodes.name: Introduce the trial functional $\bar A(a,b)$
nodes.statement: We introduce \be \bar A(a,b):= \frac {R^2}{2} (a\a+b(1-\a))-\log R-\frac12-\frac{1-2\a}{2}\log b -\frac{\a}{2}\int \r_{MP}(d\l;\a)\log(ab-(1-\a)\b^2\l)\,. \ee and $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \bar A(a,b)\,,\quad \forall a,b>0\,:\,\,ab>(1-\a)\b^2\l_+\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Define the trial free energy $\bar A(a,b)$ and record that it bounds the limsup for every admissible $a,b$.

nodes.name: Convexity gives the upper bound
nodes.statement: A direct inspection shows that $A(a,b)$ is jointly uniformly convex for any $\a\in[0,1/2]$ if $ab>(1-\a)\b^2\l_+$, therefore \be \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2}A_{N_1,N_2}\leq \min_{ab>(1-\a)\b^2\l_+} \bar A(a,b)\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: Joint uniform convexity for $\a\in[0,1/2]$ lets one minimise over $a,b$.

nodes.name: Record the gradient of $\bar A$
nodes.statement: We record for later use the gradient coordinates \bea \partial_a \bar A(a,b)&=&\frac{\a R^2}{2}-\frac\a2\int \r_{MP}(d\l;\a)\frac{b}{ab- (1-\a)\b^2\l}\,;\\ \partial_b \bar A(a,b)&=&\frac{(1-\a)R^2}{2} -\frac{1-2\a}{2b}-\frac\a2\int \r_{MP}(d\l;\a)\frac{a}{ab- (1-\a)\b^2\l}\,. \eea
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\partial_a\bar A$ and $\partial_b\bar A$ for later use.

nodes.name: Set up the reverse bound with shells
nodes.statement: For the reverse bound consider again spherical shells around $S_{R,N_1}$ and $S_{R,N_2}$ of thickness $\e$, that we name respectively $S_{1,\e}$ and $S_{2,\e}$. We split $S_{1,\e}=\R^{N_1}\setminus S^c_{1,\e}$ and $S_{2,\e}=\R^{N_2}\setminus S^c_{2,\e}$ and set $S_{\e}:=S_{1,\e}\times S_{2,\e}$. We have \bea \e^2 \widehat Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}&:=&\e^2\int\s_{N_1, R,\e}(dx)\s_{N_2,R,\e}(dy)e^{-\b H_N(x,y)}\nn\\ &=&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{\R^{N_1}\times \R^{N_2}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\nn\\ &-&\exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)\right) \int_{S^c_{\e}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M_i z_i)\right)\,, \eea where we used again the representation (\ref{eq:repr-Z-RBM}).
nodes.statement_short: Write the doubly shelled partition function as a full integral minus the complement.

nodes.name: Four-region decomposition of the complement
nodes.statement:
The free energy associated to the first summand was already computed above in the thermodynamic limit. Therefore we have to upper bound the second summand. We consider four contributions according to the following decomposition. Let $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and put  ea S_\e^{\kappa,1}&:=&\{x\in\R^{N_1}\,, y\in\R^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|x\|^2-R^2N_1)\geq \e N_1\,\}\,,
n\ S_\e^{\kappa,2}&:=&\{x\in\R^{N_1}\,, y\in\R^{N_2}\,:\,\, \kappa(\|y\|^2-R^2N_2)\geq \e N_2\,\}\,.
n \eea Thus $S_\e^c= igcup_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}}S_\e^{\kappa,j}$. Moreover we pick $\eta>0$ small enough and set  ea M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) &:=& \left( { egin{array}{cc} a+(2-j)\kappa\eta & - \sqrt{1-\a}\s_i \ - \sqrt{1-\a}\s_i & b+(j-1)\kappa\eta \ \end{array} } ight)\,,\quad i\in[N_1]
n\ M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta)&:=&\diag(0,b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)\,,\quad i=N_1+1,\ldots , N_2\,.
n \eea
nodes.statement_short: Cover the shell complement by four regions indexed by $\kappa$ and layer $j$, each with its own tilted matrix.

nodes.name: Tilted partition functions for each region
nodes.statement: Also, we put \bea Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}^{\kappa,j}&:=& \exp\left(\frac {R^2}{2} (aN_1+b N_2)+\frac{(2-j)N_1\kappa\eta a}{2}+\frac{(j-1)N_2\kappa\eta b}{2}-\eta \e N_j\right)\nn\\ &&\int_{S_\e^{\kappa,j}} \frac{dxdy}{|S_1||S_2|}\exp\left( -\frac 1 2 \sum_{i=1}^{N_2} (z_i^T,M^{(\kappa,j)}_i(\eta) z_i)\right)\nn\\ \eea so that $$ (\ref{eq:II-termRBM})=-\sum_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j=1,2} Z_{N_1,N_2,\e}^{\kappa,j}\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Define the tilted partition function on each region so that their sum reproduces the complement term.

nodes.name: Lower bound by a maximum of tilted functionals
nodes.statement:
We conclude that for any $\eta>0$ sufficiently small and $a,b$ with $ab>(1-\a) ^2\l_+$  e \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} \widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\geq \max( ar A(a,b), \{A_\e^{\kappa, j}(\eta; a,b)\}_{\kappa\in\{-1,1\},j\in\{1,2\}})\,, \ee where  ea A_\e^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)&:=&-\eta\e+ rac12\a a(R^2+(2-j)\kappa\eta)+ rac12(1-\a) b(R^2+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
n\ &-&\log R - rac12- rac{1-2\a}{2}\log (b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
n\ &-& rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\log((a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\a) ^2\l)\,. 
n \eea
nodes.statement_short: The shell free energy is bounded below by the max of $\bar A$ and the four tilted functionals $A_\e^{\kappa,j}$.

nodes.name: Derivative test on the differences $\D_\e^{\kappa,j}$
nodes.statement:
In analogy with the proof of Theorem ef{Th:HM-sfer} we define  ea \D_{\e}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)&:=& ar A(a,b)-A_\e^{\kappa,j}(\eta; a,b)
n\ &=&\eta \e-(2-j)\kappa rac{\eta\a a}{2}-(j-1)\kappa rac{\eta(1-\a) b}{2}+ rac{1-2\a}{2}\log(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)
n\ &+& rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\log\left( rac{(a+(2-j)\kappa\eta)(b+(j-1)\kappa\eta)- (1-\a) ^2\l}{ab-(1-\a) ^2\l}ight)\,.
n \eea We need to show that $\D_{\e}^{\kappa,j}(\eta)\geq0$ for $\eta>0$ small. As before, to do so it suffices to prove the derivative in the origin to be non-negative uniformly in $\e>0$. Bearing in mind (ef{eq:grad1RBM}), (ef{eq:grad2RBM}) we have  ea  rac{d}{d\eta} \D_{\e}^{\kappa,j}(\eta) ig|_{\eta=0}&=&\e+(2-j)\kappa\left(- rac{a\a R^2}{2}+ rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\left( rac{b}{ab-(1-\a) ^2\l}ight)ight)
n\ &+&(j-1)\kappa\left(- rac{b(1-\a) R^2}{2}+ rac{1-2\a}{2b}+ rac\a2 \int _{MP}(d\l;\a)\left( rac{a}{ab-(1-\a) ^2\l}ight)ight)
n\ &=&\e-(2-j)\kappa\partial_a ar A-(j-1)\kappa\partial_b ar A\geq0\,. 
n \eea
nodes.statement_short: Non-negativity of $\D_\e^{\kappa,j}$ reduces to the sign of $\e$ minus the gradient of $\bar A$.

nodes.name: Conclude at the minimiser of $\bar A$
nodes.statement: Since the inequality must hold for any $\e>0$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$, we have to pick $(\bar a, \bar b)=\arg\min \bar A$. Therefore $$ \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\geq \max(\bar A(\bar a,\bar b), \{A^{\e,\kappa_1,\kappa_2}(\eta; \bar a,\bar b)\}_{\kappa_1,\kappa_2\in\{-1,1\}})= \min_{ab>\b^2(1-\a)\l_+}\bar A( a, b)\quad \forall \e>0\,, $$ which combined with (\ref{eq:upperbound.RBM}) proves the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Requiring the inequality for all $\e,\kappa,j$ forces $(\bar a,\bar b)=\arg\min\bar A$, matching the upper bound.

nodes.name: Existence of the free energy of $RBM_{\s,\g}$
nodes.statement: Let $A_N$ be the free energy of $RBM_{\s,\g}$. Then $\lim_NA_N$ exists $P$-a.s.
assumptions: Let $A_N$ be the free energy of $RBM_{\s,\g}$.

nodes.name: A priori bound for the free energy of $HM_\r$
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ be the free energy of $HM_{\r}$. There is $f(\l_+,\b)$ continuous and bounded for which \be \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\l_+,\b)\,. \ee
assumptions: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ be the free energy of $HM_{\r}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the a priori bound for $HM_\r$
nodes.statement:
Let $a>\l_+$ and set for brevity $\l^*:=\max_{i\in[N_1]}\l_i$. We write $$  rac{1}{N_1+N_2}E[\log Z_{N_1,N_2}]=\sum_{k\geq0}E\left[ rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \l^*> kaight ]P((k+1)a\geq \l^*> ka)\,. $$ Inside the conditional expectation we can bound $ H_N(z)\leq a\|z\|^2\, $. Therefore  ea E\left[ rac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \l^*> kaight]&\leq&  rac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log\int\g_{N_1,	heta}(dx) \exp\left(\|x\|^2(  a(k+1))-Nr\left( rac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}ight)ight)
n\ &\leq& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(  a(k+1))-N_1r\left( rac{R}{\sqrt N_1}ight)ight)\,
n\ &=&\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(  a(k+1))-r\left(Right)ight)\,.
n \eea On the other hand by assumption  e P((k+1)a\geq \l^*> ka)\leq 2e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\,,\quad c>0\,. \ee In conclusion  e E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq \sum_{k\geq0}e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(  a(k+1))-r\left(Right)ight)=:f(a, )\,, \ee a continuous bounded function. In particular the estimate holds also for $a	o\l_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Condition on dyadic-type blocks of the top eigenvalue, bound the energy by $a\|z\|^2$ on each, and sum the resulting Gaussian tail series.

nodes.name: Condition on the size of the top eigenvalue
nodes.statement: Let $a>\l_+$ and set for brevity $\l^*:=\max_{i\in[N_1]}\l_i$. We write $$ \frac{1}{N_1+N_2}E[\log Z_{N_1,N_2}]=\sum_{k\geq0}E\left[\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \l^*> ka\right ]P((k+1)a\geq \l^*> ka)\,. $$
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the expected free energy over the events $(k+1)a\ge\l^*>ka$.

nodes.name: Bound the conditional free energy
nodes.statement:
Inside the conditional expectation we can bound $ H_N(z)\leq a\|z\|^2\, $. Therefore  ea E\left[ rac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log Z_{N_1,N_2}\,|\,\,(k+1)a\geq \l^*> kaight]&\leq&  rac{1}{N_1+N_2} \log\int\g_{N_1,	heta}(dx) \exp\left(\|x\|^2(  a(k+1))-Nr\left( rac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N}ight)ight)
n\ &\leq& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(  a(k+1))-N_1r\left( rac{R}{\sqrt N_1}ight)ight)\,
n\ &=&\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(  a(k+1))-r\left(Right)ight)\,.
n \eea
nodes.statement_short: On each event bound $H_N(z)\le a\|z\|^2$ and maximise the exponent over the radius.

nodes.name: Gaussian bound on the conditioning probabilities
nodes.statement: On the other hand by assumption \be P((k+1)a\geq \l^*> ka)\leq 2e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\,,\quad c>0\,. \ee
nodes.statement_short: The sub-Gaussian assumption gives $e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}$ decay for each block.

nodes.name: Sum the series
nodes.statement: In conclusion \be E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq \sum_{k\geq0}e^{-ca^2k^2N_1}\max_{R\geq0}\left(R^2(\b a(k+1))-r\left(R\right)\right)=:f(a,\b)\,, \ee a continuous bounded function. In particular the estimate holds also for $a\to\l_+$.
nodes.statement_short: The resulting series converges to a continuous bounded $f(a,\b)$, valid up to $a\to\l_+$.

nodes.name: A priori bound for the free energy of $RBM_{\r^2}$
nodes.statement: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ be the free energy of $RBM_{\r^2}$. There is $f(\l_+,\b)$ continuous and bounded for which \be \lim\sup_{N_1,N_2} E[A_{N_1,N_2}]\leq f(\l_+,\b)\,. \ee
assumptions: Let $A_{N_1,N_2}$ be the free energy of $RBM_{\r^2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the a priori bound for $RBM_{\r^2}$
nodes.statement: Same proof as before, noting \bea \b(1-\a)\sum_{i}\s_ix_iy_i-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt {N_1}}, \frac{\|y\|}{\sqrt {N_2}}\right)&\leq& \b(1-\a)a\|x\|\|y\|-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt {N_1}}\right)\nn\\ &\leq&\max_{R_1,R_2}\left(\b(1-\a)aR_1R_2-r(R_1,R_2)\right)\,\nn \eea for any $a>\s_+$.
nodes.statement_short: Identical to the $HM_\r$ argument once the bilinear energy is bounded by $\b(1-\a)a\|x\|\|y\|$ against the two-layer regulariser.

nodes.name: Configurations far outside the typical ball are negligible
nodes.statement_short: For all three priors, the partition-function mass outside a ball of radius $R N^{(1+\d)/2}$ decays like $e^{-cN_1^{1+\d}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of the tail estimate
nodes.statement: We prove only (\ref{eq:coda1}), as (\ref{eq:coda2}), (\ref{eq:coda3}) are similar. Let us write \bea \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\d}\}} \r(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}&\leq& e^{-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\d}}{2\theta}}\int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\d}\}} \g_{N_1,2\theta}(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)-N_1r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}\right)}\nn\\ &\leq&e^{-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\d}}{2\theta}} Z_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta) =\exp\left( (N_1+N_2)A_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta)-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\d}}{2\theta}\right)\,. \nn \eea Here we have emphasised the dependence on $\theta$ of partition function and free energy. Then (\ref{eq:coda1}) follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:apriori-bound-HM}.
nodes.statement_short: Trade half of the Gaussian density for the factor $e^{-R^2N_1^{1+\d}/2\theta}$, leaving a partition function controlled by the a priori bound.

nodes.name: Extract the Gaussian tail factor
nodes.statement: We prove only (\ref{eq:coda1}), as (\ref{eq:coda2}), (\ref{eq:coda3}) are similar. Let us write \bea \int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\d}\}} \r(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}&\leq& e^{-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\d}}{2\theta}}\int_{\{\|x\|^2\geq R^2N_1^{1+\d}\}} \g_{N_1,2\theta}(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)-N_1r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}\right)}\nn\\ &\leq&e^{-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\d}}{2\theta}} Z_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta) =\exp\left( (N_1+N_2)A_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta)-\frac{R^2N_1^{1+\d}}{2\theta}\right)\,. \nn \eea
nodes.statement_short: Split the Gaussian density to pull out $e^{-R^2N_1^{1+\d}/2\theta}$ and leave $Z_{N_1,N_2}(2\theta)$.

nodes.name: Apply the a priori bound
nodes.statement: Here we have emphasised the dependence on $\theta$ of partition function and free energy. Then (\ref{eq:coda1}) follows from Lemma \ref{lemma:apriori-bound-HM}.
nodes.statement_short: The a priori free-energy bound makes the remaining factor subexponential in $N_1^{1+\d}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem \ref{th:main} (Legendre equivalences)
nodes.statement:
Now we are ready to prove the Legendre equivalences of Theorem ef{th:main}. We shall prove only (ef{eq:mainHM}), (ef{eq:mainRBM1}), (ef{eq:mainRBM2}); the dual relations (ef{eq:mainHM-dual}), (ef{eq:mainRBM1-dual}), (ef{eq:mainRBM2-dual}) then follow directly, as one can easily verify the inverse Legendre transformation to be also well defined and involutive. We start by $i)$, where we deal with a single Gaussian prior. Let $\e>0$, $\d>0$. From now on we will systematically omit the dependence on $\d$ of the objects we will operate with. Let further $r<N_1^{\d}/\e$, $R_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\d}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\d})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\e$, and decompose $ \R^{N_1}:= igcup_{i=0}^rS^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}\cup T $, where $$ S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}:=\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\quad T:=\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\d+ rac12}\}\,. $$ Comparing with (ef{eq:Sfshell}) one easily sees that the $S^{[i]}_{\e,N_1}$ are spherical shells. We denote by $\s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}$ the uniform distributions on these shells. Then we have  e Z^{}_{N_1,N_1}=\sum_{i=0}^r Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}[i]+	ilde Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}\,, \ee where $$ Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}}_{N_1}(dx)e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,,\quad 	ilde Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}:=\int_{T}_{N_1}(dx)e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,. $$ The tail term $	ilde Z^_{N_1,N_2}$ gives a negligible contribution thanks to Lemma ef{lemma:coda} and we will ignore it all the time. Thus by (ef{eq:dec}) we get $$ \max_{i\in[r]} Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\leq Z^{}_{N_1,N_2, }\leq  rac{N^{\d}}{\e}\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\,. $$ Therefore setting  e A_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\left( rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}[i]ight) \ee we have  e \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]ight)\leq  rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{}_{N_1,N_2}\leq \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]ight)+ rac{\d\log N_1-\log \e}{N_1+N_2}\,. \ee So the free energy of $HM_{}$ is given by the limit of $\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]ight)$, provided it exists. We notice now that by continuity for any $x\in S^{[i]}_{\e,N_1}$  e  rac{\|x\|^2}{2	heta}+N_1r\left( rac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}ight)= rac{	ilde R_i^2N_1}{2	heta}+N_1r\left(	ilde R_iight)+\OOO{\e} \ee where $	ilde R_i\in[R_i, R_{i+1}]$. Therefore  e Z^{}_{N_1,N_2, }[i]=e^{- rac{	ilde R_i^2N_1}{2	heta}-N_1r\left(	ilde R_i ight)-\OOO{\e}} rac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}|}{\sqrt{2\pi	heta}^{N_1}}\int \s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}(dx)e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\, \ee and  ea A_{N_1,N_2}[i]&=& rac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\left( rac{1}{N_1}\log\left( rac{|S^{[i]}_{\e,N_1}|}{\sqrt{2\pi	heta}^{N_1}}ight)- rac{	ilde R_i^2}{2	heta }-r\left(	ilde R_iight)ight)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}^{\e}\left(	ilde R_iight)+ rac{\OOO{\e}}{N_1+N_2}
n\ &=:&	ilde A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\left(	ilde R_iight)+ rac{\OOO{\e}}{N_1+N_2}
n\,. \eea Thus we see that the existence of the thermodynamic limit is ensured by Lemma ef{lemma-gusci} and we have $$ \lim_{N_1,N_2}\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]ight)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{N_1,N_2}\left(	ilde A_{N_1,N_2,\e}(R)ight)=:\sup_{R>0}	ilde A_\e(R)\,. $$ By the uniform concavity of $	ilde A_\e(R)$ we have $$ \lim_{\e	o0}\sup_{R>0}	ilde A_\e(R)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{\e	o0}	ilde A_\e(R)=- rac{\a}{2}\log	heta+\a\sup_{R>0}\left(\log R+ rac12+\a^{-1}A_{\s}(R, )-r(R)- rac{R^2}{2	heta}ight)\, $$ and the proof of (ef{eq:mainHM}) is concluded. \ Note that in this argument the regularising function $r$ plays essentially no role. So it can be set to zero and repeat verbatim all the previous steps for the $RBM_{\s,\g}$. This way we obtain (ef{eq:mainRBM1}). \ Finally we turn to $RBM_{^2}$. Here we have to slice up both Gaussian priors and the previous construction easily extends. We just sketch the argument, stressing only the points in which it differs from above. Let $\e>0$, $\d>0$, $r<N_1^{\d}/\e$, $r'<N_2^{\d}/\e$, $R_0,R'_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\d}$, $R'_{r'+1}:=N_2^{\d}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\d})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\e$, $\{R'_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r'}\subset[0,N_2^{\d})$ with $|R'_{i+1}-R'_i|<2\e$. Decompose $ \R^{N_1}	imes \R^{N_2}:= igcup_{i\in[r], j\in[r']}S_{N_1,\e}^{[i]}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]} \cup T $, where  ea S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}&:=&\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,
n\ {S'}^{[i]}_{N_2,\e}&:=&\{z\in\R^{N_2}\,\:\, R'_i\sqrt{N_2}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R'_{i+1}\sqrt{N_2}\}\,,
n\ T&:=&\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\d+ rac12}\}\cup \{z\in\R^{N_2}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_2}^{\d+ rac12}\}\,.
n \eea Again $T$ can be neglected due to Lemma ef{lemma:coda}. We have to evaluate  ea &&Z^{^2}_{N_1,N_2}[i,j]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]}}^2_{N_1N_2}(dxdy)e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,
n\ &=& rac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi	heta}^{N_1+N_2}} e^{- rac{	ilde R^2_iN_1+{R'}^2_jN_2}{2	heta}-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(	ilde{R}_i, 	ilde{R'}_jight)+\OOO{\e}} \int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_1,\e}^{[j]}}\s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}(dx)\s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}(dy) e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,
n \eea where the $	ilde R_i$ and $	ilde {R'}_i$ are introduced as before (see (ef{eq:Rtilde})). Therefore  ea A_{N_1,N_2, }[i,j]&:=& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{^2}_{N_1,N_2, }[i,j]
n\ &=& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log\left( rac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi	heta}^{N_1+N_2}}ight)+ rac{\OOO{\e}}{N_1+N_2} - rac{	ilde R^2_i+{R'}^2_j}{2	heta}
n\ &-& rac{\sqrt{N_1N_2}}{N_1+N_2}r\left(	ilde R_i, 	ilde {R'}_jight)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}(	ilde R_i, 	ilde R_j)
n\,, \eea where $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}(	ilde R_i, 	ilde {R'}_j)$ is the free energy of the RBM whose priors are the spherical shell measures of centres $	ilde R_i, 	ilde {R'}_j$. The argument to pass to the thermodynamic limit is then the same, so (ef{eq:mainRBM2}) is obtained.
nodes.statement_short: Slice $\R^{N_1}$ (and $\R^{N_2}$) into shells of thickness $\e$, so that the Gaussian partition function becomes a max over shell radii of the spherical free energy plus the radial cost, then let $\e\to0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to the three direct relations
nodes.statement: Now we are ready to prove the Legendre equivalences of Theorem \ref{th:main}. We shall prove only (\ref{eq:mainHM}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2}); the dual relations (\ref{eq:mainHM-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM1-dual}), (\ref{eq:mainRBM2-dual}) then follow directly, as one can easily verify the inverse Legendre transformation to be also well defined and involutive.
nodes.statement_short: Only the three forward identities need proof; the duals follow since the Legendre transform is involutive here.

nodes.name: Slice $\R^{N_1}$ into spherical shells
nodes.statement: We start by $i)$, where we deal with a single Gaussian prior. Let $\e>0$, $\d>0$. From now on we will systematically omit the dependence on $\d$ of the objects we will operate with. Let further $r<N_1^{\d}/\e$, $R_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\d}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\d})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\e$, and decompose $ \R^{N_1}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^rS^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}\cup T $, where $$ S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}:=\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,\quad T:=\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\d+\frac12}\}\,. $$ Comparing with (\ref{eq:Sfshell}) one easily sees that the $S^{[i]}_{\e,N_1}$ are spherical shells. We denote by $\s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}$ the uniform distributions on these shells.
nodes.statement_short: Partition $\R^{N_1}$ into $O(N_1^\d/\e)$ shells plus a far tail $T$.

nodes.name: Decompose the partition function and drop the tail
nodes.statement: Then we have \be Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_1}=\sum_{i=0}^r Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}[i]+\tilde Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}\,, \ee where $$ Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}}\r_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,,\quad \tilde Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}:=\int_{T}\r_{N_1}(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\,. $$ The tail term $\tilde Z^\r_{N_1,N_2}$ gives a negligible contribution thanks to Lemma \ref{lemma:coda} and we will ignore it all the time.
nodes.statement_short: Split $Z^\r$ into shell contributions plus a tail that is negligible by the tail lemma.

nodes.name: Sandwich the free energy by the largest shell
nodes.statement: Thus by (\ref{eq:dec}) we get $$ \max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\leq Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2,\b}\leq \frac{N^{\d}}{\e}\max_{i\in[r]} Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\,. $$ Therefore setting \be A_{N_1,N_2}[i]:=\left(\frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right) \ee we have \be \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)\leq \frac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2}\leq \max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)+\frac{\d\log N_1-\log \e}{N_1+N_2}\,. \ee So the free energy of $HM_{\r}$ is given by the limit of $\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)$, provided it exists.
nodes.statement_short: The number of shells is subexponential, so the free energy equals the max over shells up to $o(1)$.

nodes.name: Factor out the radial cost of each shell
nodes.statement: We notice now that by continuity for any $x\in S^{[i]}_{\e,N_1}$ \be \frac{\|x\|^2}{2\theta}+N_1r\left(\frac{\|x\|}{\sqrt N_1}\right)=\frac{\tilde R_i^2N_1}{2\theta}+N_1r\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\OOO{\e} \ee where $\tilde R_i\in[R_i, R_{i+1}]$. Therefore \be Z^{\r}_{N_1,N_2,\b}[i]=e^{-\frac{\tilde R_i^2N_1}{2\theta}-N_1r\left(\tilde R_i \right)-\OOO{\e}}\frac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1}}\int \s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}(dx)e^{-\b H_{N_1,N_2}(x)}\, \ee and \bea A_{N_1,N_2}[i]&=&\frac{N_1}{N_1+N_2}\left(\frac{1}{N_1}\log\left(\frac{|S^{[i]}_{\e,N_1}|}{\sqrt{2\pi\theta}^{N_1}}\right)-\frac{\tilde R_i^2}{2\theta }-r\left(\tilde R_i\right)\right)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2}^{\e}\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\frac{\OOO{\e}}{N_1+N_2}\nn\\ &=:&\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\e}\left(\tilde R_i\right)+\frac{\OOO{\e}}{N_1+N_2}\nn\,. \eea
nodes.statement_short: On each shell the Gaussian weight and regulariser are constant up to $O(\e)$, leaving a spherical-shell free energy times a radial factor.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit and obtain relation i)
nodes.statement: Thus we see that the existence of the thermodynamic limit is ensured by Lemma \ref{lemma-gusci} and we have $$ \lim_{N_1,N_2}\max_{i\in[r]}\left(A_{N_1,N_2}[i]\right)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{N_1,N_2}\left(\tilde A_{N_1,N_2,\e}(R)\right)=:\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\e(R)\,. $$ By the uniform concavity of $\tilde A_\e(R)$ we have $$ \lim_{\e\to0}\sup_{R>0}\tilde A_\e(R)=\sup_{R>0}\lim_{\e\to0}\tilde A_\e(R)=-\frac{\a}{2}\log\theta+\a\sup_{R>0}\left(\log R+\frac12+\a^{-1}A_{\s}(R,\b)-r(R)-\frac{R^2}{2\theta}\right)\, $$ and the proof of (\ref{eq:mainHM}) is concluded.
nodes.statement_short: Interchange the $\e\to0$ and $\sup_R$ limits by uniform concavity to obtain the Legendre formula for $HM_\r$.

nodes.name: Relation ii) by setting the regulariser to zero
nodes.statement: Note that in this argument the regularising function $r$ plays essentially no role. So it can be set to zero and repeat verbatim all the previous steps for the $RBM_{\s,\g}$. This way we obtain (\ref{eq:mainRBM1}).
nodes.statement_short: Setting $r\equiv0$ and repeating the argument gives the $RBM_{\s,\g}$ identity.

nodes.name: Relation iii) by slicing both layers
nodes.statement:
Finally we turn to $RBM_{^2}$. Here we have to slice up both Gaussian priors and the previous construction easily extends. We just sketch the argument, stressing only the points in which it differs from above. Let $\e>0$, $\d>0$, $r<N_1^{\d}/\e$, $r'<N_2^{\d}/\e$, $R_0,R'_0:=0$, $R_{r+1}:=N_1^{\d}$, $R'_{r'+1}:=N_2^{\d}$, $\{R_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r}\subset[0,N_1^{\d})$ with $|R_{i+1}-R_i|<2\e$, $\{R'_i\}_{i=1,\ldots,r'}\subset[0,N_2^{\d})$ with $|R'_{i+1}-R'_i|<2\e$. Decompose $ \R^{N_1}	imes \R^{N_2}:= igcup_{i\in[r], j\in[r']}S_{N_1,\e}^{[i]}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]} \cup T $, where  ea S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}&:=&\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, R_i\sqrt{N_1}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R_{i+1}\sqrt{N_1}\}\,,
n\ {S'}^{[i]}_{N_2,\e}&:=&\{z\in\R^{N_2}\,\:\, R'_i\sqrt{N_2}\leq \|z\|_2\leq R'_{i+1}\sqrt{N_2}\}\,,
n\ T&:=&\{z\in\R^{N_1}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_1}^{\d+ rac12}\}\cup \{z\in\R^{N_2}\,\:\, \|z\|_2\geq {N_2}^{\d+ rac12}\}\,.
n \eea Again $T$ can be neglected due to Lemma ef{lemma:coda}. We have to evaluate  ea &&Z^{^2}_{N_1,N_2}[i,j]:=\int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]}}^2_{N_1N_2}(dxdy)e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,
n\ &=& rac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi	heta}^{N_1+N_2}} e^{- rac{	ilde R^2_iN_1+{R'}^2_jN_2}{2	heta}-\sqrt{N_1N_2}r\left(	ilde{R}_i, 	ilde{R'}_jight)+\OOO{\e}} \int_{S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_1,\e}^{[j]}}\s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}(dx)\s^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}(dy) e^{-  H_{N_1,N_2}(x,y)}\,,
n \eea where the $	ilde R_i$ and $	ilde {R'}_i$ are introduced as before (see (ef{eq:Rtilde})). Therefore  ea A_{N_1,N_2, }[i,j]&:=& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log Z^{^2}_{N_1,N_2, }[i,j]
n\ &=& rac{1}{N_1+N_2}\log\left( rac{|S^{[i]}_{N_1,\e}	imes {S'}_{N_2,\e}^{[j]}|}{\sqrt{2\pi	heta}^{N_1+N_2}}ight)+ rac{\OOO{\e}}{N_1+N_2} - rac{	ilde R^2_i+{R'}^2_j}{2	heta}
n\ &-& rac{\sqrt{N_1N_2}}{N_1+N_2}r\left(	ilde R_i, 	ilde {R'}_jight)+\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}(	ilde R_i, 	ilde R_j)
n\,, \eea where $\widehat A_{N_1,N_2,\e}(	ilde R_i, 	ilde {R'}_j)$ is the free energy of the RBM whose priors are the spherical shell measures of centres $	ilde R_i, 	ilde {R'}_j$. The argument to pass to the thermodynamic limit is then the same, so (ef{eq:mainRBM2}) is obtained.
nodes.statement_short: Slicing both Gaussian priors into shells indexed by $(i,j)$ repeats the computation and yields the two-radius Legendre formula.
